items.text: Construction of the theory with basic set $I$ (transfinite)
$J_0$ = free category with finite products on the elements $X_i$, $i\in I$: objects $\prod X_i^{n_i}$, almost all $n_i=0$.
J_0\simeq\bigl((\text{finite sets})^{\circ}\bigr)^{(I)}\quad\text{(families of finite sets, almost all empty)}
R_0=\widehat{J_0}
Adding finite inverse limits to a discrete category = adding finite products.
\begin{CD} I @>>> J_0\\ @. @VVV\\ @. R_0 \end{CD}
$\Delta$-functors $R_0\to E$ $\;=\;$ $E^I$ $\;=\;$ product-preserving functors $J_0\to E$.
Step 2 : add axioms
Assume $R_\alpha$ built, with $J_0\to R_\alpha$ (products preserved) generating.
R_{\alpha+1}=R_\alpha[\Sigma_\alpha^{-1}]\qquad(\Sigma_\alpha\text{ small family of arrows, saturated})
Same objects as $R_\alpha$, so $J_0$ still generates.
Step 3 : add arrows
H\ \text{small set},\quad H\to\operatorname{Ob}(R_\alpha)\times\operatorname{Ob}(R_\alpha)\ \ (\text{source},\text{target})
Theory: a $\Delta$-functor $R_\alpha\to E$ plus, for each $h\in H$, an arrow in $E$ between the images of source and target.
$S\subset\operatorname{Ob}R_\alpha$: all sources and targets; $D$ the diagram $H\rightrightarrows S$; $\widetilde D$ the free category on $D$.
H\rightrightarrows S\qquad D=(S,H)
T(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R_\alpha,E)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(S,E)}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(\widetilde D,E)
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(\widetilde D,E)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(\rho(\widetilde D),E),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}(S,E)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(\rho(S),E)
$\rho$ = enveloping topos: add finite inverse limits, then the hat.
\begin{CD} \rho(S) @>>> \rho(\widetilde D)\\ @VVV @.\\ R_\alpha @. \end{CD}
R_{\alpha+1}=R_\alpha\sqcup_{\rho(S)}\rho(\widetilde D)\quad\text{(2-sum in }\Delta)
To check: $J_0$ generates $R_{\alpha+1}$, i.e. $R_\alpha\to R_{\alpha+1}$ is essentially surjective on objects.
Not surjective on arrows; not a subtopos — arrows were added, not axioms.
$\widetilde D$: objects = vertices of $D$; arrows = formal composites of paths.
$R_{\alpha+1}$ generated by images of small subcategories; $R_\alpha$ is generated by $J_0$.
Objects of $\rho(\widetilde D)$: finite products of objects of $\widetilde D$, then direct limits; products come from $S$.
So $R_\alpha$ generates $R_{\alpha+1}$ essentially on objects.
Step 4 : limit ordinals
R=2\text{-}\varinjlim_{\beta<\alpha}R_\beta\quad(\text{i.e. 2-inverse limit of the theories } T_{R_\beta})
Use small sites $C_\beta\subset R_\beta$ stable under finite inverse limits; take their 2-limit in Cat, then $\rho$.
$R$ is generated by the images of the $C_\beta$, hence of the $R_\beta$, hence by $J_0$.
So: algebraic theory with basic $I$ $\Rightarrow$ $R$ is a topos and finite products of objects of $I$ generate.
Converse
$I\to R$ with finite products of $B(i)$ generating (so $R$ a topos). Show: the theory is algebraic with base $I$ — no transfinite construction.
Steps: (1) base objects; (2) arrows between finite products; (3) axioms. Axioms may use infinite direct limits.
Step 1: empty structure on $I$: $R_0=\widehat{J_0}=\rho_{\Pi,\Delta}(J_0)$.
$\Pi$ = 2-category of categories with finite products.
Step 2: $J_1$: same objects as $J_0$, add all arrows between images in $R$, products kept products.
One base element $x$: arrows between the powers $x^i$, e.g. a composition $x^2\to x$.
R_1=\rho_{\Pi,\Delta}(J_1)
Axioms
$A,B,C\in J_0$, $\varphi\colon J_0\to R$: composite of the added arrows $A\to B\to C$ must map to the composite in $R$.
J_2=J_1/\text{(composition axioms)},\qquad R_2=\rho_{\Pi,\Delta}(J_2)
$J_2$ = full subcategory of $R$ generated by $J_0$.
T_2(E)=\{J_2\to E\ \text{compatible with products}\}\ \hookrightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,E)
Full embedding; image: functors $J_2\to E$ that are continuous, send certain inductive cones to exact cones, and extend left exactly.
$R=R_3$ obtained from $R_2$ by inverting arrows: a subtopos (surjective on objects and arrows).
Two inversions in a row = one: $R_3$ from $R_1$ by inverting a family of arrows between constructions.
Constructions in $R_1$: finite inverse limits, then arbitrary direct limits, on the finite products and added arrows.
Writing the conditions as axioms
J\subset R\ \text{generating},\quad \operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,E)\to T_{\mathrm{Cat},J}(E)\supset T_{\Pi,J}(E)
Image of $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,E)$: functors $J\to E$ that are continuous and whose extension to $R$ is left exact.
Products: for $X,Y\in J$ and $\varphi\colon J\to E$ require
\varphi(X\times Y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\varphi(X)\times\varphi(Y)
Each $X\in J$ gives a construction $\varepsilon_X\colon\varphi\mapsto\varphi(X)$ (compatible with base change in $E$).
\varepsilon_{X\times Y}\longrightarrow\varepsilon_X\times\varepsilon_Y\quad\text{(arrow between constructions)}
Axiom: this arrow between constructions becomes an isomorphism on the structures considered.
In $\Delta$ the category of constructions of a representable theory is $R$ itself: axioms = arrows of $R_2$ made invertible.
With kernels, equalising axioms reduce to making an arrow (kernel $\to$ ambient object) an isomorphism: one type of axiom suffices.
S(E)\ \supset\ S'(E)\ \supset\ \operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,E)\quad\text{(each step: adding axioms)}
$J_2\subset R$ generating, stable under finite products; theory $E\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(J_2,E)$.
$R$ is a subtopos of the enveloping topos of $J_2$ (called $R_2$).
$C$ small generating, stable under finite inverse limits: functors $C\to E$ coming from $R$ = continuous and left exact.
